questions.question: Explain why (−3)² = 9 but −3² = −9.
questions.expected_answer: With brackets the whole number −3 is squared: (−3)(−3) = 9. Without brackets the exponent applies to 3 only and the negative is attached afterwards: −(3 × 3) = −9.

questions.question: Why does √(−16) have no real answer while ∛(−27) does?
questions.expected_answer: A square is a product of two equal factors, so it is never negative; no real number squares to −16. A cube keeps the sign of its base, so (−3)³ = −27 and ∛(−27) = −3.
